newsitem.title: TURKEY: First tanker of Iraqi oil arrives at Turkish port.
newsitem.headline: First tanker of Iraqi oil arrives at Turkish port.

text.p: The first tanker to load Iraqi crude in Turkey under the U.N. oil-for-food deal arrived at the western Turkish port of Izmir on Thursday, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
The Gole tanker, loaded with 153,500 tonnes of Kirkuk crude, transported the oil from the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan to the Aliaga refinery owned by Turkey's state-owned refiner Tupras.
Anatolian said the unloading of the tanker had already begun. The United Nations last week approved Tupras' contract to buy 75,000 bpd of Iraqi oil over the six months of the deal.
Tupras has said that some of the oil purchased under the contract may also be transported to the company's Kirikkale refinery, connected by a 447-km (280-mile) pipeline to Ceyhan.
Turkey held a ceremony in Ceyhan on Monday to celebrate the loading of the tanker.
Shipping sources in London said earlier that at least three more crude oil tankers were expected to load Iraqi crude from Ceyhan before the end of this month.
Ship brokers and other sources said the 142,000 deadweight tonne (dwt) Tito Tapias had been chartered by Elf to load Iraqi crude on December 21 and was expected to sail to Lavera.

They also thought that the 142,000 dwt Marble had been chartered by Spain's Repsol to load on December 24, and added that they expected either the Oak or the Saturn to load 130,000 tonnes on December 30 with options to sail to northwest Europe or Mediterranean destinations.
One broker said he thought Shell had made the latter fixture.
Iraqi crude is also being exported from the terminal of Mina al-Bakr in southern Iraq.
